objects.description: This header defines no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes. It only contains preprocessor configuration macros for encoding selection and inlining behavior. There is no user-defined type to document.
Struct representing an IPv4 address stored as 4 octets. Suitable for holding and passing IPv4 addresses within the library.
Struct representing an IPv6 address stored as 16 octets. Suitable for holding and passing IPv6 addresses within the library.

objects.definition:
typedef struct UriMemoryManagerStruct {
    UriFuncMalloc malloc; /**< Pointer to custom malloc(3) */
    UriFuncCalloc calloc; /**< Pointer to custom calloc(3); to emulate using malloc and
                             memset see uriEmulateCalloc */
    UriFuncRealloc realloc; /**< Pointer to custom realloc(3) */
    UriFuncReallocarray reallocarray; /**< Pointer to custom reallocarray(3); to emulate
                                         using realloc see uriEmulateReallocarray */
    UriFuncFree free; /**< Pointer to custom free(3) */
    void *
        userData; /**< Pointer to data that the other function members need access to */
} UriMemoryManager; /**< @copydoc UriMemoryManagerStruct */
objects.description: Class-like struct encapsulating function pointers for custom memory management and an opaque userData pointer. Used to plug in allocator behavior throughout the library.
Function pointer type for custom malloc(3)-compatible allocation using a UriMemoryManager and size.
Function pointer type for custom calloc(3)-compatible allocation using a UriMemoryManager, nmemb, and size.
Function pointer type for custom realloc(3)-compatible reallocation using a UriMemoryManager, pointer, and new size.

objects.definition:
typedef void * (*UriFuncReallocarray)(struct UriMemoryManagerStruct *, void *, size_t,
                                      size_t);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom reallocarray(3)-compatible reallocation using a UriMemoryManager, pointer, nmemb, and size.
Function pointer type for custom free(3)-compatible deallocation using a UriMemoryManager and pointer.

objects.definition:
typedef enum UriBreakConversionEnum {
    URI_BR_TO_LF, /**< Convert to Unix line breaks ("\\x0a") */
    URI_BR_TO_CRLF, /**< Convert to Windows line breaks ("\\x0d\\x0a") */
    URI_BR_TO_CR, /**< Convert to Macintosh line breaks ("\\x0d") */
    URI_BR_TO_UNIX = URI_BR_TO_LF, /**< @copydoc UriBreakConversionEnum::URI_BR_TO_LF */
    URI_BR_TO_WINDOWS =
        URI_BR_TO_CRLF, /**< @copydoc UriBreakConversionEnum::URI_BR_TO_CRLF */
    URI_BR_TO_MAC = URI_BR_TO_CR, /**< @copydoc UriBreakConversionEnum::URI_BR_TO_CR */
    URI_BR_DONT_TOUCH /**< Copy line breaks unmodified */
} UriBreakConversion; /**< @copydoc UriBreakConversionEnum */
objects.description: Enumeration selecting a line break conversion mode for text processing (LF, CRLF, CR, or leave unchanged).

objects.definition:
typedef enum UriNormalizationMaskEnum {
    URI_NORMALIZED = 0, /**< Do not normalize anything */
    URI_NORMALIZE_SCHEME = 1 << 0, /**< Normalize scheme (fix uppercase letters) */
    URI_NORMALIZE_USER_INFO =
        1 << 1, /**< Normalize user info (fix uppercase percent-encodings) */
    URI_NORMALIZE_HOST = 1 << 2, /**< Normalize host (fix uppercase letters) */
    URI_NORMALIZE_PATH = 1 << 3, /**< Normalize path (fix uppercase percent-encodings and
                                    redundant dot segments) */
    URI_NORMALIZE_QUERY =
        1 << 4, /**< Normalize query (fix uppercase percent-encodings) */
    URI_NORMALIZE_FRAGMENT =
        1 << 5, /**< Normalize fragment (fix uppercase percent-encodings) */
    URI_NORMALIZE_PORT = 1 << 6 /**< Normalize port (drop leading zeros) @since 0.9.9 */
} UriNormalizationMask; /**< @copydoc UriNormalizationMaskEnum */
objects.description: Bitmask enumeration indicating which URI components should be normalized (scheme, user info, host, path, query, fragment, port).
Bitmask/flags controlling how URI references are resolved, with strict RFC behavior or a compatibility mode for identical scheme handling.
Alias for int used as a boolean type throughout the library; typical values are URI_TRUE (1) and URI_FALSE (0).
Built-in type pointer; not a custom type. Ignored per instructions.
URI_CHAR is referenced but not defined in this header; it is defined in UriDefsAnsi.h/UriDefsUnicode.h. Per instructions, referenced-only types are ignored.

Text range type representing a half-open interval [first, afterLast) within a URI string. Used across URI components such as scheme, host text, query, fragment, and within path segments. Details like encoding (A/W) are controlled by inclusion pass macros and URI_CHAR.
Linked-list node for a URI path segment. Each node stores the segment text and a pointer to the next segment. The reserved field is internal to the parser.

Structured host representation accompanying hostText: either ip4, ip6, or IPvFuture text (registered name is represented with all-zero members). When used inside Uri, ipFuture must alias hostText memory.

objects.definition:
typedef struct URI_TYPE(UriStruct) {
    URI_TYPE(TextRange) scheme; /**< Scheme (e.g. "http") */
    URI_TYPE(TextRange) userInfo; /**< User info (e.g. "user:pass") */
    URI_TYPE(TextRange)
    hostText; /**< Host text (set for all hosts, excluding square brackets) */
    URI_TYPE(HostData) hostData; /**< Structured host type specific data */
    URI_TYPE(TextRange) portText; /**< Port (e.g. "80") */
    URI_TYPE(PathSegment) * pathHead; /**< Head of a linked list of path segments */
    URI_TYPE(PathSegment) * pathTail; /**< Tail of the list behind pathHead */
    URI_TYPE(TextRange) query; /**< Query without leading "?" */
    URI_TYPE(TextRange) fragment; /**< Query without leading "#" */
    UriBool absolutePath; /**< Absolute path flag, distincting "a" and "/a"; always
                             <c>URI_FALSE</c> for URIs with host */
    UriBool owner; /**< Memory owner flag */

    void * reserved; /**< Reserved to the parser */
} URI_TYPE(Uri);
objects.description: Primary URI object per RFC 3986 with ranges for components, linked-list path, host details, and ownership flags. Memory ownership and normalization are controlled via API functions in this header. The reserved field is internal to the parser.
Parsing context used by legacy ParseUri* APIs; points to a target Uri to be filled and stores error information. The reserved field is internal.
Linked-list node representing a single key/value pair from the query string. Value may be NULL. Used by compose/dissect query APIs.

functions.name: uriCompleteMemoryManager
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriCompleteMemoryManager(UriMemoryManager * memory, UriMemoryManager * backend);
functions.description: Wraps a backend UriMemoryManager that may only provide malloc(3) and free(3) into a complete memory manager by filling in calloc, realloc, reallocarray, and free/malloc wrappers that manage an internal size header. Use when you need a fully-populated UriMemoryManager interface without implementing realloc/reallocarray yourself. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: memory must be a valid, writable pointer (OUT) where the completed manager will be written; it must not be NULL.
backend must be a valid pointer (IN) to a UriMemoryManager providing at least malloc and free; it must not be NULL.
Callers must not rely on the internal behavior of the functions assigned to memory->malloc/free/realloc, as they are considered internal and may change.
On non-zero return, the caller must treat setup as failed and not use the partially-initialized memory manager.

functions.name: uriEmulateCalloc
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC void * uriEmulateCalloc(UriMemoryManager * memory, size_t nmemb, size_t size);
functions.description: Emulates calloc(3) using memory->malloc and memset: allocates nmemb * size bytes and zero-initializes the result. Returns a pointer to zeroed memory on success or NULL on failure. Useful when only malloc is available in a UriMemoryManager.
requirements: memory must be a valid pointer to an initialized UriMemoryManager; it should not be NULL.
nmemb is the number of elements; size is the size in bytes per element; both are inputs and may be zero or non-zero per calloc semantics (behavior for zero sizes follows the underlying allocator).
If the function returns NULL, the caller must treat it as allocation failure and not dereference the pointer.
ptr returned must later be freed using memory->free of the same memory manager.

functions.name: uriEmulateReallocarray
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC void * uriEmulateReallocarray(UriMemoryManager * memory, void * ptr, size_t nmemb, size_t size);
functions.description: Emulates reallocarray(3) on top of memory->realloc: resizes an allocation for an array of nmemb elements of size bytes each. Returns a pointer to the resized allocation or NULL on failure. If ptr is NULL, behaves like allocation; if nmemb or size are zero, behavior follows reallocarray semantics as implemented via memory->realloc.
requirements: memory must be a valid pointer to an initialized UriMemoryManager; it should not be NULL.
ptr must be either NULL or a pointer previously allocated using the same memory manager (memory->malloc/memory->realloc/...); passing foreign or stack pointers is invalid.
nmemb is the number of elements; size is the size in bytes per element; both are inputs.
On NULL return, the original ptr remains valid and owned by the caller (per realloc-like semantics); the caller must check for NULL before using the result.
The returned pointer, when non-NULL, must be freed with memory->free of the same memory manager.

functions.name: uriTestMemoryManager
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriTestMemoryManager(UriMemoryManager * memory);
functions.description: Runs a suite of allocation/reallocation/free tests against the given UriMemoryManager to validate basic correctness (including preserving data across realloc). Intended for diagnostics; returns 0 on success or an error code on failure (e.g., URI_ERROR_MEMORY_MANAGER_FAULTY).
requirements: memory must be a valid pointer to an initialized UriMemoryManager; it should not be NULL.
Caller should interpret a non-zero return as test failure and not use the memory manager in production without investigation.

functions.name: uriTestMemoryManagerEx
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriTestMemoryManagerEx(UriMemoryManager * memory, UriBool challengeAlignment);
functions.description: Extended memory-manager test suite. Like uriTestMemoryManager, but can optionally challenge pointer alignment when challengeAlignment is non-zero. Returns 0 on success or an error code on failure.
requirements: memory must be a valid pointer to an initialized UriMemoryManager; it should not be NULL.
challengeAlignment selects whether tests also verify alignment-sensitive behavior; any non-zero value enables extra checks.
Caller should interpret a non-zero return as test failure and address the reported issues before use.

functions.name: uriParseIpFourAddressA
functions.signature: int uriParseIpFourAddressA(unsigned char *octetOutput, const char *first, const char *afterLast);
functions.description: Parses an IPv4 address given as ANSI text and converts it into four octets. The function reads characters in the half-open range [first, afterLast) and writes the resulting 4-byte IPv4 address to octetOutput. Returns 0 on success and a non-zero error code on failure. Typical use is to pass pointers to the start and end of a substring containing only the IPv4 address in dotted-decimal form.
requirements: octetOutput must be non-null and point to at least 4 bytes of writable memory.
first and afterLast must be non-null pointers into the same contiguous char buffer; afterLast must be greater than or equal to first.
The substring [first, afterLast) should contain a valid IPv4 text representation (commonly dotted-decimal) and be the span to parse.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value indicates an error.
Input must be ANSI (narrow) characters; use the W variant for wide characters.

functions.name: uriParseIpFourAddressW
functions.signature: int uriParseIpFourAddressW(unsigned char *octetOutput, const wchar_t *first, const wchar_t *afterLast);
functions.description: Parses an IPv4 address given as wide-character text and converts it into four octets. The function reads characters in the half-open range [first, afterLast) and writes the resulting 4-byte IPv4 address to octetOutput. Returns 0 on success and a non-zero error code on failure. Typical use is to pass pointers to the start and end of a substring containing only the IPv4 address in dotted-decimal form.
requirements: octetOutput must be non-null and point to at least 4 bytes of writable memory.
first and afterLast must be non-null pointers into the same contiguous wchar_t buffer; afterLast must be greater than or equal to first.
The substring [first, afterLast) should contain a valid IPv4 text representation (commonly dotted-decimal) and be the span to parse.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; any non-zero value indicates an error.
Input must be wide characters (wchar_t); use the A variant for narrow characters.

functions.name: uriHasHostA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC UriBool uriHasHostA(const UriUriA * uri)
functions.description: Returns whether the given URI has a host component set. Use for quick presence checks before operations that require a host.
requirements: uri must be a valid, initialized UriUriA pointer (can be NULL only if caller expects URI_FALSE).

functions.name: uriHasHostW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC UriBool uriHasHostW(const UriUriW * uri)
functions.description: Wide-char variant of uriHasHostA. Returns whether the given URI has a host component set.
requirements: uri must be a valid, initialized UriUriW pointer (can be NULL only if caller expects URI_FALSE).

functions.name: uriParseIpSixAddressA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseIpSixAddressA(UriIp6 * output, const char * first, const char * afterLast)
functions.description: Parses an IPv6 address text in [first, afterLast) into 16-byte representation in output. Uses default libc memory manager.
requirements: first must point to the first character of IPv6 text; afterLast to one past the last character.
output may be NULL (parses/validates without writing).
Returns URI_SUCCESS (0) on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriParseIpSixAddressW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseIpSixAddressW(UriIp6 * output, const wchar_t * first, const wchar_t * afterLast)
functions.description: Wide-char variant of uriParseIpSixAddressA. Parses IPv6 text into 16-byte representation.
requirements: first must point to the first wide character of IPv6 text; afterLast to one past the last character.
output may be NULL.
Returns URI_SUCCESS (0) on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriParseIpSixAddressMmA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseIpSixAddressMmA(UriIp6 * output, const char * first, const char * afterLast, UriMemoryManager * memory)
functions.description: Parses an IPv6 address text into 16 bytes using the provided memory manager (NULL for default libc).
requirements: first and afterLast delimit the input range.
memory may be NULL to use default libc.
output may be NULL.
Returns URI_SUCCESS (0) on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriParseIpSixAddressMmW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseIpSixAddressMmW(UriIp6 * output, const wchar_t * first, const wchar_t * afterLast, UriMemoryManager * memory)
functions.description: Wide-char, memory-manager variant of IPv6 parsing.
requirements: first and afterLast delimit the input range.
memory may be NULL to use default libc.
output may be NULL.
Returns URI_SUCCESS (0) on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriParseUriExA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseUriExA(UriParserStateA * state, const char * first, const char * afterLast)
functions.description: Deprecated. Parses a URI from [first, afterLast) into state->uri using the default libc memory manager.
requirements: state must not be NULL and must have state->uri set to an output UriUriA.
first must not be NULL; afterLast must not be NULL.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.
Prefer uriParseSingleUriExA.

functions.name: uriParseUriExW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseUriExW(UriParserStateW * state, const wchar_t * first, const wchar_t * afterLast)
functions.description: Wide-char deprecated parser that fills state->uri from [first, afterLast).
requirements: state must not be NULL and have state->uri set.
first and afterLast must not be NULL.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.
Prefer uriParseSingleUriExW.

functions.name: uriParseUriA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseUriA(UriParserStateA * state, const char * text)
functions.description: Deprecated. Parses a zero-terminated URI string text into state->uri using default libc memory manager.
requirements: state must not be NULL and must have state->uri set.
text must not be NULL.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.
Prefer uriParseSingleUriA.

functions.name: uriParseUriW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseUriW(UriParserStateW * state, const wchar_t * text)
functions.description: Wide-char deprecated parse-from-string into state->uri.
requirements: state must not be NULL and have state->uri set.
text must not be NULL.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.
Prefer uriParseSingleUriW.

functions.name: uriParseSingleUriA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseSingleUriA(UriUriA * uri, const char * text, const char ** errorPos)
functions.description: Parses a single RFC 3986 URI from a zero-terminated string using default libc memory manager.
requirements: uri must not be NULL and must be an initialized UriUriA to receive output.
text must not be NULL.
errorPos may be NULL; if provided and return is URI_ERROR_SYNTAX, *errorPos is set to the first offending character.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriParseSingleUriW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseSingleUriW(UriUriW * uri, const wchar_t * text, const wchar_t ** errorPos)
functions.description: Wide-char variant to parse a single URI from a zero-terminated wide string.
requirements: uri must not be NULL.
text must not be NULL.
errorPos may be NULL; set only when returning URI_ERROR_SYNTAX.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriParseSingleUriExA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseSingleUriExA(UriUriA * uri, const char * first, const char * afterLast, const char ** errorPos)
functions.description: Parses a single URI from [first, afterLast) (afterLast may be NULL to use strlen(first)); default libc memory manager.
requirements: uri must not be NULL.
first must not be NULL.
afterLast can be NULL to imply first + strlen(first).
errorPos may be NULL; set only when returning URI_ERROR_SYNTAX.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriParseSingleUriExW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseSingleUriExW(UriUriW * uri, const wchar_t * first, const wchar_t * afterLast, const wchar_t ** errorPos)
functions.description: Wide-char range-based single URI parser; afterLast may be NULL to use first + wcslen(first).
requirements: uri must not be NULL.
first must not be NULL.
afterLast can be NULL to imply end by wcslen.
errorPos may be NULL; set only when returning URI_ERROR_SYNTAX.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriParseSingleUriExMmA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseSingleUriExMmA(UriUriA * uri, const char * first, const char * afterLast, const char ** errorPos, UriMemoryManager * memory)
functions.description: Parses a single URI from [first, afterLast) using a provided memory manager (NULL for default libc).
requirements: uri must not be NULL.
first must not be NULL; afterLast may be NULL to imply end by strlen.
errorPos may be NULL; set only when returning URI_ERROR_SYNTAX.
memory may be NULL for default libc.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriParseSingleUriExMmW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriParseSingleUriExMmW(UriUriW * uri, const wchar_t * first, const wchar_t * afterLast, const wchar_t ** errorPos, UriMemoryManager * memory)
functions.description: Wide-char, memory-managed range-based single URI parser.
requirements: uri must not be NULL.
first must not be NULL; afterLast may be NULL.
errorPos may be NULL; set only when returning URI_ERROR_SYNTAX.
memory may be NULL for default libc.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriFreeUriMembersA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC void uriFreeUriMembersA(UriUriA * uri)
functions.description: Frees all memory associated with the members of the URI structure (but not the structure itself) using default libc memory manager. Safe to call on zero-initialized structures.
requirements: uri must point to a UriUriA structure. It is safe to pass an all-zeros structure.
Do not call on an uninitialized structure.

functions.name: uriFreeUriMembersW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC void uriFreeUriMembersW(UriUriW * uri)
functions.description: Wide-char variant. Frees member allocations of the UriUriW (structure itself not freed).
requirements: uri must point to a UriUriW structure; safe to call on all-zeros.
Do not call on an uninitialized structure.

functions.name: uriFreeUriMembersMmA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriFreeUriMembersMmA(UriUriA * uri, UriMemoryManager * memory)
functions.description: Frees members of UriUriA using the provided memory manager (NULL for default libc).
requirements: uri must point to a UriUriA; safe on all-zeros, unsafe on uninitialized.
memory may be NULL for default libc.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriFreeUriMembersMmW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriFreeUriMembersMmW(UriUriW * uri, UriMemoryManager * memory)
functions.description: Wide-char variant: frees members of UriUriW using provided memory manager.
requirements: uri must point to a UriUriW; safe on all-zeros, unsafe on uninitialized.
memory may be NULL for default libc.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriEscapeExA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC char * uriEscapeExA(const char * inFirst, const char * inAfterLast, char * out, UriBool spaceToPlus, UriBool normalizeBreaks)
functions.description: Percent-encodes all but unreserved characters from [inFirst, inAfterLast) into out. Optionally converts spaces to '+' and normalizes line breaks to CRLF (encoded).
requirements: inFirst points to input start; inAfterLast points one past end.
out must have sufficient capacity: at least 3x input length if normalizeBreaks==URI_FALSE, 6x if URI_TRUE.
spaceToPlus controls ' '→'+'.
normalizeBreaks controls CR/LF normalization.
Returns pointer to the terminator position in out.

functions.name: uriEscapeExW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC wchar_t * uriEscapeExW(const wchar_t * inFirst, const wchar_t * inAfterLast, wchar_t * out, UriBool spaceToPlus, UriBool normalizeBreaks)
functions.description: Wide-char variant of uriEscapeExA. Note: wchar_t units are treated as code points 0x01..0xFF; arbitrary Unicode input will not produce proper results.
requirements: inFirst/inAfterLast delimit input.
out capacity: ≥3x input length if normalizeBreaks==URI_FALSE, ≥6x if URI_TRUE.
spaceToPlus and normalizeBreaks behave as in A variant.
Returns pointer to the terminator position in out.

functions.name: uriEscapeA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC char * uriEscapeA(const char * in, char * out, UriBool spaceToPlus, UriBool normalizeBreaks)
functions.description: Percent-encodes all but unreserved characters from zero-terminated input string in to out. Convenience wrapper around uriEscapeExA.
requirements: in must be non-NULL zero-terminated.
out must have sufficient capacity as noted for uriEscapeExA.
spaceToPlus and normalizeBreaks control behavior.
Returns pointer to the terminator position in out.

functions.name: uriEscapeW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC wchar_t * uriEscapeW(const wchar_t * in, wchar_t * out, UriBool spaceToPlus, UriBool normalizeBreaks)
functions.description: Wide-char variant of uriEscapeA with same caveats about Unicode handling as uriEscapeExW.
requirements: in must be non-NULL zero-terminated.
out must be sufficiently large (see uriEscapeExW).
Returns pointer to the terminator position in out.

functions.name: uriUnescapeInPlaceExA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC const char * uriUnescapeInPlaceExA(char * inout, UriBool plusToSpace, UriBreakConversion breakConversion)
functions.description: In-place decoding of percent-encoded sequences in inout, optionally converting '+' to space and applying line break conversion. Returns pointer to new terminating zero.
requirements: inout may be NULL (function returns NULL).
plusToSpace controls '+'→' ' conversion.
breakConversion selects line break conversion mode.
Operate on mutable buffer as transformation is in-place.

functions.name: uriUnescapeInPlaceExW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC const wchar_t * uriUnescapeInPlaceExW(wchar_t * inout, UriBool plusToSpace, UriBreakConversion breakConversion)
functions.description: Wide-char variant of in-place unescape with options for '+' and line breaks.
requirements: inout may be NULL (returns NULL).
In-place modification requires writable buffer.

functions.name: uriUnescapeInPlaceA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC const char * uriUnescapeInPlaceA(char * inout)
functions.description: In-place unescape of percent-encoded sequences. Does not convert '+' to space, does not normalize line breaks. Returns pointer to new terminator.
requirements: inout may be NULL (returns NULL).
Buffer must be writable.

functions.name: uriUnescapeInPlaceW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC const wchar_t * uriUnescapeInPlaceW(wchar_t * inout)
functions.description: Wide-char variant of simple in-place unescape (no '+' or break conversion).
requirements: inout may be NULL (returns NULL).
Buffer must be writable.

functions.name: uriAddBaseUriA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriAddBaseUriA(UriUriA * absoluteDest, const UriUriA * relativeSource, const UriUriA * absoluteBase)
functions.description: Resolves a relative reference against an absolute base per RFC 3986 §5.2.2, storing result in absoluteDest. Uses default libc memory manager. Caller must free absoluteDest members on success.
requirements: absoluteDest is output UriUriA to hold result; on success caller must call uriFreeUriMembersA on it.
relativeSource is the reference to resolve; may be same as dest only if API allows (not stated).
absoluteBase is the base URI to resolve against.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriAddBaseUriW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriAddBaseUriW(UriUriW * absoluteDest, const UriUriW * relativeSource, const UriUriW * absoluteBase)
functions.description: Wide-char variant of resolving relative reference against base using default memory manager. Caller frees dest members on success.
requirements: absoluteDest is output; free members with uriFreeUriMembersW on success.
relativeSource and absoluteBase are inputs.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriAddBaseUriExA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriAddBaseUriExA(UriUriA * absoluteDest, const UriUriA * relativeSource, const UriUriA * absoluteBase, UriResolutionOptions options)
functions.description: Resolves a reference against a base with configurable options; default libc memory manager. Caller frees dest members on success.
requirements: absoluteDest is output; free members with uriFreeUriMembersA on success.
relativeSource and absoluteBase are inputs.
options supplies resolution configuration.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriAddBaseUriExW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriAddBaseUriExW(UriUriW * absoluteDest, const UriUriW * relativeSource, const UriUriW * absoluteBase, UriResolutionOptions options)
functions.description: Wide-char variant of reference resolution with options.
requirements: absoluteDest is output; free members on success.
Provide appropriate options.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise error code.

functions.name: uriAddBaseUriExMmA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriAddBaseUriExMmA(UriUriA * absoluteDest, const UriUriA * relativeSource, const UriUriA * absoluteBase, UriResolutionOptions options, UriMemoryManager * memory)
functions.description: Resolves a reference against a base with options using a provided memory manager (NULL for default). Caller must free dest members with uriFreeUriMembersMmA on success.
requirements: absoluteDest is output; on success free members with uriFreeUriMembersMmA using the same memory manager.
relativeSource and absoluteBase are inputs.
options configures resolution.
memory may be NULL for default libc.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriAddBaseUriExMmW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriAddBaseUriExMmW(UriUriW * absoluteDest, const UriUriW * relativeSource, const UriUriW * absoluteBase, UriResolutionOptions options, UriMemoryManager * memory)
functions.description: Wide-char, memory-managed reference resolution with options. Caller must free dest members with uriFreeUriMembersMmW on success.
requirements: absoluteDest is output; free members with matching memory manager.
relativeSource and absoluteBase are inputs.
memory may be NULL for default libc.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise error code.

functions.name: uriRemoveBaseUriA
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriRemoveBaseUriA(UriUriA * dest, const UriUriA * absoluteSource, const UriUriA * absoluteBase, UriBool domainRootMode)
functions.description: Attempts to create a relative reference for absoluteSource against absoluteBase (or keep absolute if scheme/authority differ). Default libc memory manager; caller must free dest members on success.
requirements: dest is output; on success caller must call uriFreeUriMembersA.
absoluteSource and absoluteBase are inputs.
domainRootMode controls path relative to domain root.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise an error code.

functions.name: uriRemoveBaseUriW
functions.signature: URI_PUBLIC int uriRemoveBaseUriW(UriUriW * dest, const UriUriW * absoluteSource, const UriUriW * absoluteBase, UriBool domainRootMode)
functions.description: Wide-char variant of making a relative reference from an absolute URI. Caller frees dest members on success.
requirements: dest is output; free with uriFreeUriMembersW on success.

NEWLINES = ['\n', '\r', '\r\n']

def _rand_octet(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias towards interesting edge values but also cover full range
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(OCTET_EDGE_VALUES)
    return rng.randint(0, 255)


def _octet_to_str(o: int, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce canonical decimal without leading zeros most of the time,
    # but occasionally use intentional leading zeros to test well-formedness
    # handling in functions that accept dotted-decimal per RFC 3986 (host IPv4
    # usually forbids leading zeros implying octal; many libraries still accept
    # them — keep both flavors but prefer valid canonical forms for setters).
    s = str(o)
    if rng.random() < 0.1 and len(s) > 0:
        # add up to 2 leading zeros (still valid text for uriParseIpFourAddressW
        # which parses IPv4 numbers as decimals). Keep length <= 3.
        pad = rng.randint(1, 2)
        s = ('0' * pad + s)[-3:]
    return s


def gen_ipv4(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    octets = [_rand_octet(rng) for _ in range(4)]
    return DOT.join(_octet_to_str(o, rng) for o in octets)


def gen_noise(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Generate ASCII noise that remains ASCII when widened. Avoid percent or '+'
    # as they are irrelevant here; include spaces, punctuation, letters, digits.
    alphabet = (
        'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
        'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ'
        '0123456789'
        ' '  # space
        '\t'  # tab
        '._-/:;,@[](){}'
    )
    n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def gen_context_with_ipv4(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a buffer that the stub will fully convert to wchar_t and then select
    # arbitrary [first, afterLast). To maximize chances that selected span
    # forms a valid IPv4 when needed, include several IPv4 tokens separated by
    # benign delimiters, plus optional leading/trailing whitespace or newlines.
    pieces: List[str] = []

    # Optional prologue noise
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        pieces.append(gen_noise(rng, 64))

    # Insert between 1 and 5 IPv4s
    count = rng.randint(1, 5)
    for i in range(count):
        # Optional whitespace/newlines before token
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            pieces.append(rng.choice(WS + NEWLINES))
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                pieces.append(rng.choice(WS))
        # Maybe wrap in brackets to test host literal surroundings in other APIs
        wrap = rng.random() < 0.2
        if wrap:
            pieces.append('[')
        ip = gen_ipv4(rng)
        pieces.append(ip)
        if wrap:
            pieces.append(']')
        # Optional trailing punctuation/whitespace
        if i != count - 1:
            sep = rng.choice([' ', '\t', '\n', ',', ';', ' '])
            pieces.append(sep)

    # Optional epilogue noise
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        pieces.append(gen_noise(rng, 64))

    s = ''.join(pieces)

    # Ensure not empty; ensure total length cap
    if not s:
        s = gen_ipv4(rng)
    if len(s) > MAX_TOTAL_LEN:
        s = s[:MAX_TOTAL_LEN]
    return s


def gen_minimal_valid(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # A small, always-valid IPv4
    fixed = ["0.0.0.0", "127.0.0.1", "255.255.255.255", "1.2.3.4", "192.168.0.1"]
    return rng.choice(fixed)


def gen_edge_ipv4_strings(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Edge forms that are still valid dotted-decimal (no hex/oct), plus
    # surrounding whitespace/newlines.
    candidates = [
        "0.0.0.0",
        "255.255.255.255",
        "001.002.003.004",  # leading zeros variant
        "10.0.0.1",
        "1.0.0.0",
        "192.0.2.1",  # TEST-NET-1
        "198.51.100.42",  # TEST-NET-2
        "203.0.113.7",  # TEST-NET-3
    ]
    core = rng.choice(candidates)
    pre = ''
    post = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pre = rng.choice(['', ' ', '\t', '\n'])
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        post = rng.choice(['', ' ', '\t', '\n'])
    return pre + core + post


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a strategy to create interesting but valid input
    strategy = rng.random()
    if strategy < 0.25:
        s = gen_minimal_valid(rng)
    elif strategy < 0.70:
        s = gen_context_with_ipv4(rng)
    else:
        s = gen_edge_ipv4_strings(rng)

    # The fuzz stubs expect FUZZ_PARAM_STR bytes that are widened to wchar_t by
    # casting each unsigned char to wchar_t. So we must ensure all bytes are in
    # 0..255. Our string s is ASCII; encode as latin-1 to keep bytes identical.
    b = s.encode('latin-1', errors='ignore')

    # Cap to fuzzer stub expectations (they may truncate further). Keep <= 4096.
    if len(b) > MAX_TOTAL_LEN:
        b = b[:MAX_TOTAL_LEN]

    return b

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for wide-char IPv6 text. The fuzz stubs take arbitrary bytes,
# convert each byte to a single wchar_t code unit (0..255), and pass the
# contiguous buffer [first, afterLast) to IPv6-related functions. We therefore
# only need to emit ASCII-range characters to control the produced wchar_t
# sequence. No NUL terminator is required; the stubs pass explicit length.
#
# We aim to cover diverse valid IPv6 forms (without brackets):
# - Full 8 groups
# - Compressed with :: at various positions
# - Leading zeros and mix of upper/lower hex
# - IPv4-embedded forms (v4-mapped, v4-compatible)
# - Zone IDs (scope) after % (e.g., %eth0) — many parsers support RFC 6874 style
# - Edge cases like empty (for stubs that sometimes pass NULL we still provide non-empty)
#
# The script returns bytes; the harness interprets them as 8-bit values and casts
# to wchar_t, so ASCII text is preserved.

HEX_LC = "0123456789abcdef"
HEX_UC = "0123456789ABCDEF"


def _rand_hex_group(r: random.Random, width_min=1, width_max=4, upper_mix=True) -> str:
    w = r.randint(width_min, width_max)
    s = "".join(r.choice(HEX_LC + (HEX_UC if upper_mix else "")) for _ in range(w))
    # ensure not empty and not all non-hex (guaranteed by choices)
    return s


def _full_ipv6(r: random.Random) -> str:
    groups = [ _rand_hex_group(r, 1, 4) for _ in range(8) ]
    return ":".join(groups)


def _compressed_ipv6(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build between 1 and 7 groups around a ::
    left_count = r.randint(0, 7)
    right_count = r.randint(0, 7 - left_count)
    left = [ _rand_hex_group(r) for _ in range(left_count) ]
    right = [ _rand_hex_group(r) for _ in range(right_count) ]
    left_s = ":".join(left)
    right_s = ":".join(right)
    if left_s and right_s:
        return f"{left_s}::${right_s}".replace("$", "")  # placeholder handling
    elif left_s:
        return f"{left_s}::"
    elif right_s:
        return f"::{right_s}"
    else:
        return "::"


def _ipv4(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return ".".join(str(r.randint(0, 255)) for _ in range(4))


def _v4_Embedded(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create an IPv6 with last 32 bits as IPv4 dotted decimal.
    # Choose 0..6 hex groups before the IPv4, possibly with compression.
    n_groups = r.randint(1, 6)  # at least one group looks more realistic
    groups = [ _rand_hex_group(r) for _ in range(n_groups) ]
    v4 = _ipv4(r)
    # Decide where to place compression (::). Allowed when total groups < 7
    # We let one occurrence of :: replace some missing groups.
    use_comp = r.choice([True, False])
    if use_comp:
        # place :: either at start, middle, or before the IPv4
        position = r.randint(0, n_groups)  # number of groups on left side
        left = groups[:position]
        right = groups[position:]
        left_s = ":".join(left)
        right_s = ":".join(right)
        if left_s and right_s:
            core = f"{left_s}::{right_s}"
        elif left_s:
            core = f"{left_s}::"
        elif right_s:
            core = f"::{right_s}"
        else:
            core = "::"
    else:
        core = ":".join(groups)
    if core.endswith(":"):
        return f"{core}{v4}"
    elif core == "":
        return v4  # unlikely but keep branch safe
    else:
        return f"{core}:{v4}"


def _with_zone(r: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    # RFC 6874 suggests %25 encoded; many implementations accept literal %
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        sep = "%25"  # encoded '%'
    else:
        sep = "%"
    # simple zone value: alnum and punctuation like ._-:/
    zchars = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789._-:/"
    zlen = r.randint(1, 8)
    zone = "".join(r.choice(zchars) for _ in range(zlen))
    return base + sep + zone


def _valid_samples() -> List[str]:
    # A curated set of canonical valid inputs to ensure coverage.
    return [
        # Full forms
        "2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334",
        "FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF",
        "0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001",
        # Compressed
        "::1",
        "2001:db8::1",
        "2001:db8:0:0:8d3:0:0:0",
        "::",
        # IPv4-embedded
        "::ffff:192.0.2.128",
        "2001:db8::192.0.2.33",
        # Mixed case
        "DeAd:BeEf::Cafe",
        # With zone (both percent and %25)
        "fe80::1%eth0",
        "fe80::a:b:c:d%25wlan0",
    ]


def _generate_ipv6_string(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Occasionally pick from curated set for guaranteed validity.
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        s = r.choice(_valid_samples())
    else:
        kind = r.choices(
            ["full", "comp", "v4"], weights=[3, 4, 3], k=1
        )[0]
        if kind == "full":
            s = _full_ipv6(r)
        elif kind == "comp":
            s = _compressed_ipv6(r)
        else:
            s = _v4_Embedded(r)
        # Randomly add a zone id to link-zone handling paths
        if r.random() < 0.25:
            s = _with_zone(r, s)
    # Random cosmetic variations
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        # randomly upper/lower case hex letters
        s2 = []
        for ch in s:
            if ch.isalpha() and ch in "abcdefABCDEF" and r.random() < 0.5:
                s2.append(ch.upper() if ch.islower() else ch.lower())
            else:
                s2.append(ch)
        s = "".join(s2)
    # Limit to 1024 chars as stub truncates; our strings are short anyway
    return s[:1024]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    s = _generate_ipv6_string(r)
    # Return as bytes (ASCII). All characters used are within ASCII.
    b = s.encode('ascii', 'strict')
    # Ensure non-empty to avoid early bailout in some stubs
    if not b:
        b = b"::1"
    # Cap size to 4096 per requirement (well under in practice)
    return b[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Target data type: URI string
# We generate zero-terminated friendly byte sequences (ASCII) that represent
# valid and diverse RFC 3986 URIs or references, as well as file: URIs that
# are acceptable for filename conversion functions. We keep size <= 4096.

SCHEMES = [
    "http", "https", "ftp", "file", "ws", "wss", "mailto", "urn",
    "tel", "ldap", "git", "ssh", "news"
]

# Some valid hosts
REG_HOSTS = [
    "example.com", "sub.example.com", "localhost", "xn--bcher-kva.example",
    "a-b.c-d", "test", "EXAMPLE.com"
]

IPV4S = [
    "127.0.0.1", "0.0.0.0", "255.255.255.255", "192.168.0.1", "10.0.1.2"
]

IPV6S = [
    "::1", "2001:db8::1", "fe80::1%25eth0", "2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334",
    "[2001:db8::7]"  # already bracketed form for authority
]

IPFUTURES = [
    "v1.aBc-._~!$&'()*+,;=:",  # generic ipfuture literal tail (to be wrapped with [])
]

PATH_SEGMENTS = [
    "", "a", "b", "..", ".", "foo", "bar", "%2F", "with%20space", "mix-._~",
]

QUERIES = [
    "", "a=b", "k=v&x=y", "q=hello+world", "empty=", "percent=%2F%3F", "multi=a&a=b",
]

FRAGMENTS = [
    "", "top", "section-1", "frag%20space", "line%0D%0Aend"
]


def _rand_choice(rnd: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return arr[rnd.randrange(len(arr))]


def _rand_port(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # include some with leading zeros (normalization target)
    options = ["", ":80", ":443", ":00022", ":65535", ":1"]
    return _rand_choice(rnd, options)


def _build_authority(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # userinfo (optional)
    userinfo_opts = ["", f"{_rand_userinfo(rnd)}@"]
    userinfo = _rand_choice(rnd, userinfo_opts)

    kind = rnd.randrange(5)
    if kind == 0:
        host = _rand_choice(rnd, REG_HOSTS)
    elif kind == 1:
        host = _rand_choice(rnd, IPV4S)
    elif kind == 2:
        # raw IPv6 without brackets in list; ensure bracketed for authority
        addr = _rand_choice(rnd, IPV6S)
        if addr.startswith("["):
            host = addr
        else:
            host = f"[{addr}]"
    elif kind == 3:
        # IPvFuture like [v1....]
        host = f"[v1.{_rand_choice(rnd, IPFUTURES)}]"
    else:
        # registered name with percent and unicode punycode-like label
        host = _rand_choice(rnd, REG_HOSTS)

    port = _rand_port(rnd)
    return f"{userinfo}{host}{port}"


def _rand_userinfo(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    base = ["user", "user:pass", "name:Pa%3Ass", "u%20n:p%40w"]
    return _rand_choice(rnd, base)


def _build_path(rnd: random.Random, absolute: bool) -> str:
    seg_count = rnd.randint(0, 4)
    segs = [_rand_choice(rnd, PATH_SEGMENTS) for _ in range(seg_count)]
    core = "/".join(segs)
    if absolute:
        return "/" + core if core != "" else "/"
    else:
        return core


def _maybe(q: str) -> bool:
    return len(q) > 0


def _compose_query(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    q = _rand_choice(rnd, QUERIES)
    return ("?" + q) if _maybe(q) else ""


def _compose_fragment(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    f = _rand_choice(rnd, FRAGMENTS)
    return ("#" + f) if _maybe(f) else ""


def _build_http_like(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    scheme = _rand_choice(rnd, ["http", "https"]) if rnd.random() < 0.8 else _rand_choice(rnd, SCHEMES)
    authority = _build_authority(rnd)
    path = _build_path(rnd, absolute=True)
    query = _compose_query(rnd)
    frag = _compose_fragment(rnd)
    return f"{scheme}://{authority}{path}{query}{frag}"


def _build_relative_ref(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # relative path reference (no scheme/authority)
    absolute = rnd.random() < 0.5
    path = _build_path(rnd, absolute=absolute)
    query = _compose_query(rnd)
    frag = _compose_fragment(rnd)
    return f"{path}{query}{frag}" if path else (query + frag if (query or frag) else ".")


def _build_mailto(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    local = _rand_choice(rnd, ["user", "first.last", "u%20ser"])  # allow percent
    domain = _rand_choice(rnd, REG_HOSTS)
    query = _rand_choice(rnd, ["", "?subject=Hi", "?subject=Hi&body=Hello%0D%0AWorld"])
    return f"mailto:{local}@{domain}{query}"


def _build_file_unix(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # For uriUriStringTo* Filename functions, produce file: URIs that map cleanly
    abs_path = _build_path(rnd, absolute=True)
    return f"file://{_rand_choice(rnd, ['localhost',''])}{abs_path}"


def _build_windows_file(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # e.g., file:///C:/Windows/System32 or file://server/share/path
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        drive = rnd.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
        parts = ["", "", "", f"{drive}:"] + [seg for seg in ["Windows", "System32", "Temp", "Program Files"] if rnd.random() < 0.6]
        path = "/".join(parts)
        return f"file://{path}"
    else:
        server = "server" if rnd.random() < 0.5 else _rand_choice(rnd, REG_HOSTS)
        share = _rand_choice(rnd, ["share", "data", "Public"])  # will percent encode spaces when API converts
        tail = _build_path(rnd, absolute=False)
        return f"file://{server}/{share}{('/' + tail) if tail else ''}"


def _build_urn(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    nid = _rand_choice(rnd, ["uuid", "isbn", "example"])  # not strictly validated by uriparser APIs
    nss = _rand_choice(rnd, [
        "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
        "9780306406157",
        "a-b_c.%2F~"
    ])
    frag = _compose_fragment(rnd)
    return f"urn:{nid}:{nss}{frag}"


def _mutate_case_normalization_targets(rnd: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Introduce uppercase in scheme/host to trigger normalization paths downstream
    if "://" in s:
        scheme, rest = s.split("://", 1)
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            scheme = scheme.upper()
        # host until next / ? #
        host_end = len(rest)
        for sep in ["/", "?", "#"]:
            idx = rest.find(sep)
            if idx != -1:
                host_end = min(host_end, idx)
        host = rest[:host_end]
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            host = host.upper()
        s = scheme + "://" + host + rest[host_end:]
    return s


def _ensure_non_empty(s: str) -> str:
    return s if s else "http://example.com/"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    builders = [
        _build_http_like,
        _build_relative_ref,
        _build_mailto,
        _build_file_unix,
        _build_windows_file,
        _build_urn,
    ]

    # Choose one or compose multiple variants occasionally by concatenating whitespace/newline-free inputs
    s = builders[rnd.randrange(len(builders))](rnd)

    # Occasionally bias towards inputs helpful for filename extraction fuzzers
    if rnd.random() < 0.25:
        s = _build_file_unix(rnd)
    if rnd.random() < 0.15:
        s = _build_windows_file(rnd)

    # Add query/fragment if missing and beneficial
    if ("?" not in s) and rnd.random() < 0.4:
        s += _compose_query(rnd)
    if ("#" not in s) and rnd.random() < 0.3:
        s += _compose_fragment(rnd)

    # Case tweaks to trigger normalization paths in parsers/serializers
    s = _mutate_case_normalization_targets(rnd, s)

    # Length guard and return as bytes (ASCII)
    s = _ensure_non_empty(s)
    if len(s) > 4096:
        s = s[:4096]
    return s.encode('ascii', 'strict')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets ANSI text inputs for uriparser functions in the fuzz stubs.
# It crafts valid, interesting strings that exercise percent-encoding/decoding,
# filename-to-URI conversions, and query dissection. It avoids malformed encodings
# where appropriate to keep inputs valid and meaningful.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~"
UNRESERVED = SAFE_CHARS
RESERVED = ":/?#[]@!$&'()*+,;="
SPACES = [" ", "\t"]
LINE_BREAKS = ["\n", "\r", "\r\n"]
HEX = "0123456789ABCDEF"

def _pct_encode_byte(b: int) -> str:
    return "%" + HEX[(b >> 4) & 0xF] + HEX[b & 0xF]

def _random_unreserved(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return r.choice(UNRESERVED)

def _random_reserved(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return r.choice(RESERVED)

def _make_valid_percent_sequences(r: random.Random, count: int) -> str:
    # Produce count percent-encoded bytes, including edge values
    res = []
    for i in range(count):
        if i == 0:
            b = 0  # %00
        elif i == 1:
            b = 0x20  # space
        elif i == 2:
            b = 0x7F  # DEL
        elif i == 3:
            b = ord('+')
        else:
            b = r.randrange(0, 256)
        res.append(_pct_encode_byte(b))
    return ''.join(res)

def _make_query_kv(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a query component with valid percent-encodings, plus signs, and spaces
    keys = ["q", "param", "user", "id", "_", "name", "value"]
    key = r.choice(keys)
    value_parts: List[str] = []
    # mix of unreserved, reserved (encoded), spaces, pluses and percent sequences
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.25:
            value_parts.append(_random_unreserved(r) * r.randint(1, 3))
        elif choice < 0.45:
            # add literal plus or space to test plusToSpace
            value_parts.append(r.choice(['+', ' ']))
        elif choice < 0.7:
            # valid percent sequences
            value_parts.append(_make_valid_percent_sequences(r, r.randint(1, 2)))
        elif choice < 0.85:
            # line breaks (to test normalization)
            value_parts.append(r.choice(LINE_BREAKS))
        else:
            # reserved characters left as-is (valid in query)
            value_parts.append(_random_reserved(r))
    value = ''.join(value_parts)
    return f"{key}={value}"

def _make_query_string(r: random.Random) -> str:
    n = r.randint(1, 5)
    parts = [_make_query_kv(r) for _ in range(n)]
    # also sprinkle leading or trailing ampersands safely sometimes
    sep = '&'
    s = sep.join(parts)
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        s = sep + s
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        s = s + sep
    return s

def _make_general_text(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    out: List[str] = []
    for i in range(length):
        p = r.random()
        if p < 0.35:
            out.append(_random_unreserved(r))
        elif p < 0.55:
            out.append(_random_reserved(r))
        elif p < 0.7:
            out.append(r.choice(SPACES))
        elif p < 0.82:
            out.append(r.choice(LINE_BREAKS))
        elif p < 0.9:
            out.append(_make_valid_percent_sequences(r, 1))
        else:
            # add a multi-byte percent sequence cluster
            out.append(_make_valid_percent_sequences(r, r.randint(2, 4)))
    s = ''.join(out)
    # ensure non-empty
    if not s:
        s = _random_unreserved(r)
    return s

def _make_unix_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Try generating both absolute and relative UNIX paths with segments that may need encoding
    is_abs = r.random() < 0.6
    seg_count = r.randint(1, 6)
    segs = []
    for _ in range(seg_count):
        # include spaces and special chars to exercise encoding
        seg = []
        for __ in range(r.randint(1, 8)):
            p = r.random()
            if p < 0.5:
                seg.append(_random_unreserved(r))
            elif p < 0.7:
                seg.append(r.choice([' ', '#', '%', '?']))
            elif p < 0.85:
                seg.append('.')
            else:
                # include a literal byte represented via percent-encoding-like text, but filenames are raw
                b = r.randrange(32, 127)
                seg.append(chr(b))
        # avoid empty segment accidental
        s = ''.join(seg) or 'x'
        segs.append(s)
    path = '/'.join(segs)
    if is_abs:
        path = '/' + path
    # Optionally append trailing slash
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        path += '/'
    return path

def _make_windows_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate absolute or relative Windows paths
    is_abs = r.random() < 0.7
    drive = chr(r.randrange(ord('A'), ord('Z') + 1)) + ':' if is_abs else ''
    seg_count = r.randint(1, 5)
    segs = []
    for _ in range(seg_count):
        seg = []
        for __ in range(r.randint(1, 8)):
            p = r.random()
            if p < 0.55:
                seg.append(_random_unreserved(r))
            elif p < 0.75:
                seg.append(r.choice([' ', '#', '%']))
            elif p < 0.85:
                seg.append('.')
            else:
                seg.append(chr(r.randrange(33, 126)))
        s = ''.join(seg) or 'x'
        # Avoid characters invalid in Windows filenames where possible, but leave some for coverage
        s = s.replace('"', '').replace('<', '').replace('>', '').replace('|', '')
        segs.append(s)
    sep = '\\'
    path = (drive + sep if drive else '') + sep.join(segs)
    # sometimes UNC path
    if not drive and r.random() < 0.1:
        path = '\\' + '\\' + 'server' + sep + 'share' + sep + path
    return path

def _assemble_pool(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    pool: List[bytes] = []
    # 1) General text rich in characters for uriEscape/Unescape
    pool.append(_make_general_text(r, 8, 256).encode('latin1', 'ignore'))
    # 2) Query strings for uriDissectQuery*
    pool.append(_make_query_string(r).encode('latin1', 'ignore'))
    # 3) Pure percent-encoded sequences and plus/space combos
    combo = []
    combo.append(_make_valid_percent_sequences(r, r.randint(3, 12)))
    combo.append(r.choice(['+', ' ']) * r.randint(1, 5))
    combo.append(_make_valid_percent_sequences(r, r.randint(1, 6)))
    pool.append(''.join(combo).encode('latin1', 'ignore'))
    # 4) Unix filename
    pool.append(_make_unix_filename(r).encode('latin1', 'ignore'))
    # 5) Windows filename
    pool.append(_make_windows_filename(r).encode('latin1', 'ignore'))
    # 6) Short fragments and userinfo-like strings
    frag = []
    frag.append(_make_general_text(r, 1, 32))
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        frag.append('/' + _make_general_text(r, 1, 16))
    pool.append(''.join(frag).encode('latin1', 'ignore'))
    # Ensure all non-empty
    pool = [p if p else b"x" for p in pool]
    return pool

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    pool = _assemble_pool(r)
    # Select one candidate emphasizing diversity per seed
    choice = r.randrange(len(pool))
    data = pool[choice]
    # Ensure size within limit
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets wide-char focused stubs which derive wchar_t input
# from raw bytes via (wchar_t)(unsigned char)byte. Provide bytes that,
# when mapped to 0x00..0xFF, create interesting URI-relevant patterns.
# We include:
# - Plain ASCII words and spaces
# - Reserved URI characters and percent-escape sequences
# - Line breaks variations (\n, \r, \r\n) to exercise normalizeBreaks
# - Plus signs to exercise spaceToPlus/plusToSpace paths
# - Query-like strings with & and = for dissectQuery
# - Unix and Windows-like filenames (absolute and relative)
# - Edge cases: empty segment, long segment, repeated % patterns
# - Mixed content to increase coverage

URI_UNRESERVED = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~"
URI_RESERVED = ":/?#[]@!$&'()*+,;="
HEX = "0123456789ABCDEF"

def _pct_encoded(seq: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in seq:
        b = ord(ch) & 0xFF
        out.append('%')
        out.append(HEX[(b >> 4) & 0xF])
        out.append(HEX[b & 0xF])
    return ''.join(out)

def _rand_pct_encoded(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        b = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        out.append('%')
        out.append(HEX[(b >> 4) & 0xF])
        out.append(HEX[b & 0xF])
    return ''.join(out)

def _unix_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Absolute or relative
    parts = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 5)
    for _ in range(count):
        seg_len = rng.randint(0, 8)
        # segments can be empty (//) or dot segments
        choices = [
            ''.join(rng.choice(URI_UNRESERVED) for _ in range(seg_len)),
            '.', '..',
        ]
        seg = rng.choice(choices)
        parts.append(seg)
    base = '/'.join(parts)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        base = '/' + base  # absolute
    # add some spaces and special chars
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base += rng.choice(['', ' ', '  '])
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base = base.replace(' ', '+')
    return base

def _windows_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    drive = chr(rng.randrange(ord('A'), ord('Z')+1)) + ':'
    parts = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 5)
    for _ in range(count):
        seg_len = rng.randint(1, 8)
        seg = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ' _-') for _ in range(seg_len))
        parts.append(seg)
    sep = '\\'
    path = drive + sep + sep.join(parts)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        path += sep  # trailing separator
    return path

def _query(rng: random.Random, n_pairs: int) -> str:
    pairs: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n_pairs):
        k_len = rng.randint(0, 8)
        v_len = rng.randint(0, 12)
        def mk(len_, allow_space_plus=True):
            alphabet = URI_UNRESERVED + "-"  # keep simple keys
            s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(len_))
            # occasionally insert spaces or pluses to test conversion
            if allow_space_plus and len_ > 0 and rng.random() < 0.5:
                pos = rng.randrange(0, len_)
                s = s[:pos] + rng.choice([' ', '+']) + s[pos:]
            # randomly percent-encode a slice
            if len(s) and rng.random() < 0.5:
                i = rng.randrange(0, len(s))
                s = s[:i] + _pct_encoded(s[i:i+1]) + s[i+1:]
            return s
        k = mk(k_len)
        v = mk(v_len)
        pairs.append(f"{k}={v}")
    # also include naked keys
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        pairs.append('flag')
    return '&'.join(pairs)

def _line_breaky(rng: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    # sprinkle CR, LF, CRLF
    inserts = ["\n", "\r", "\r\n"]
    s = list(base)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        pos = rng.randrange(0, len(s)+1)
        s[pos:pos] = list(rng.choice(inserts))
    return ''.join(s)

def _cases(seed: int) -> List[bytes]:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    cases: List[str] = []

    # 1. Basic ASCII text with spaces
    cases.append("Hello World")

    # 2. Reserved characters
    cases.append(URI_RESERVED)

    # 3. Mixed percent-encoded and raw
    cases.append("A" + _rand_pct_encoded(rng, 3) + "/B?c=%7E&x=1+2")

    # 4. Query-like payload
    cases.append(_query(rng, rng.randint(1, 5)))

    # 5. Unix filename absolute with spaces and dots
    cases.append(_unix_path(rng))

    # 6. Windows filename with spaces
    cases.append(_windows_path(rng))

    # 7. Line-break heavy string
    cases.append(_line_breaky(rng, "Line A Line B"))

    # 8. Plus-heavy
    cases.append("++a+b++ +c++")

    # 9. Percent-edge cases: sequence of % followed by hex/non-hex
    cases.append("%%%25%2f%GG%0D%0Aend")

    # 10. Long unreserved run then reserved
    cases.append(''.join(rng.choice(URI_UNRESERVED) for _ in range(64)) + "?#&=")

    # 11. Empty-like (but not zero-length): just NUL avoided; use dot and slashes
    cases.append("./../")

    # 12. IPv6-ish host literal to feed general text paths
    cases.append("[2001:db8::1]")

    # 13. Fragment-like
    cases.append("section-1_sub~part")

    # 14. Filename that is relative with spaces to test file converters
    cases.append("rel dir/file name.txt")

    # 15. Raw bytes 0x00-0xFF mapped via Latin-1 to stress escaping; avoid actual NUL in Python str
    raw = ''.join(chr(b) for b in range(1, 256))
    cases.append(raw)

    # Choose one deterministically-random case and optionally mutate compositionally (valid variants)
    pick = rng.randrange(0, len(cases))
    s = cases[pick]

    # Compose with optional prefix/suffix that remain valid generic text
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        prefix = rng.choice(['', '../', '/', './', 'file:', 'file:///'])
        s = prefix + s
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        suffix = rng.choice(['', '?'+_query(rng, rng.randint(1,3)), '#frag', '#'+_pct_encoded('end')])
        s = s + suffix

    # Ensure length within 1..1024 for the stubs, and overall <= 4096
    if len(s) == 0:
        s = 'x'
    if len(s) > 1024:
        s = s[:1024]

    # Return as bytes preserving 0x01..0xFF mapping; avoid embedding NUL because stubs may treat length, but some APIs expect 0-term later handle by fuzzer
    # Use latin-1 encoding to map codepoints 0..255 directly to bytes
    return s.encode('latin-1', errors='ignore')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    return _cases(seed)

def _rand_tail(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:

    s = []

        # Seed with 1 from a few buckets to diversify
        for b in buckets:
            if len(s) < n and rng.random() < 0.7:
                s.append(rng.choice(b))
        # Fill the rest
        while len(s) < n:
            b = rng.choice([UNRESERVED, SUBDELIMS, ":"])
            s.append(rng.choice(b))
        rng.shuffle(s)
    return "".join(s)


def _rand_ipvfuture(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Randomly choose uppercase or lowercase V
    v_char = rng.choice(["v", "V"]) 
    # 1*HEXDIG: choose 1..8 for variety
    ver_len = rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 2, 4, 8])

def _interesting_variants(base: str) -> List[str]:

    v: List[str] = []

    v.append(base + ":" + ":".join(["a"] * 10))
    # Tail-only unreserved
    v.append(base.split(".")[0] + "." + "a" * 64)
    # Tail-only sub-delims
    v.append(base.split(".")[0] + "." + "!$&'()*+,;=" * 5)
    # Alternating types
    v.append(base.split(".")[0] + "." + "a:!b:~c:;d")
    return v


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose strategy: corpus, corpus-variant, or random construction
    strategy = rng.random()
    candidates: List[str] = []

    if strategy < 0.35:
        # Pure corpus
        candidates = list(SEED_CORPUS)
    elif strategy < 0.7:
        # Corpus with variants
        base = rng.choice(SEED_CORPUS)
        candidates = [base] + _interesting_variants(base)

        candidates = [_rand_ipvfuture(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8))]

    if rng.random() < 0.1:
